title: Old Money vs New Money: 20 Differences
description:
There are two kinds of rich in America: old money and new money. They both have wealth, but they earn, spend and protect it very differently. In this video I go through 20 differences from three angles: the financial numbers, the psychology of status and risk, and the playbook old money families use to keep wealth for generations, plus what new money does better.

Get The Ryan Rover Money Playbook: [LINK HERE]

Chapters:
0:00 Intro
1:51 How we got the numbers
2:26 Angle 1: The Numbers
2:32 1. Assets vs income
4:10 2. Generations vs years
5:28 3. Diversified vs concentrated
7:01 4. Debt as a tool vs debt as a lifestyle
8:29 5. Tax planning vs tax surprises
9:58 6. Spending rate
11:18 7. Protection vs exposure
12:33 The Vanderbilt warning
13:47 Angle 2: The Psychology
14:00 8. Quiet vs loud
15:13 9. Quality vs brands
16:18 10. Security vs proving
17:17 11. Patience vs speed
18:31 12. Networks vs transactions
19:35 13. Identity beyond money
20:35 14. Risk appetite
21:55 Angle 3: The Playbook
22:10 15. Family meetings
23:17 16. Preparing heirs
24:19 17. Philanthropy
25:23 18. Long term holding
26:23 19. What new money does better
27:31 20. The best of both
28:32 Five classic new money mistakes
29:47 The great wealth transfer
30:37 Starting your own old money family
31:51 What to copy this year
32:22 Questions people ask
33:32 Recap: all 20 differences
34:09 What to do next

Sources:
- Roy Williams and Vic Preisser, Preparing Heirs (2003): Williams Group research on family wealth transitions (about 70% lost by generation 2, 90% by generation 3)
- UBS, Billionaire Ambitions reports (inherited vs self-made billionaire wealth)
- Ramsey Solutions, National Study of Millionaires (most millionaires first generation)
- Thomas J. Stanley, The Millionaire Next Door (1996): economic outpatient care
- Arthur T. Vanderbilt II, Fortune's Children: The Fall of the House of Vanderbilt (1989)
- IRS, basis of inherited property (step-up in basis)
- Barber and Odean, Trading Is Hazardous to Your Wealth (Journal of Finance, 2000)
- Cerulli Associates, US wealth transfer projections

Photos: Wikimedia Commons contributors. Full credits and licenses: https://github.com/ryan-rover-money-channel/ryan-rover-money/blob/main/agendamento/creditos/video30.md
